title: Risotto con Gamberi
subtitle: Prawn risotto with bisque and white wine
excerpt: Risotto con gamberi is a prawn risotto built on a quick prawn-head bisque that takes 20 minutes to make and delivers far more flavour than plain stock. The prawns cook briefly at the end so they stay tender. The result is a rich, orange-tinted risotto that tastes strongly of the sea.
sourceNotes: Prawn risotto is made along the whole Italian coastline. The technique of using prawn heads to make a quick stock is standard in Italian coastal cooking and is the key to depth of flavour in this dish.

content.text: Buy raw prawns with heads on if possible -- the heads make the stock. If only headless prawns are available, use fish stock or a light chicken stock instead. The prawn stock takes 20 minutes but makes a real difference to the finished risotto.

items.prepNote: shell-on, heads on if possible -- shells and heads reserved for stock

content.text: Peel the {{prawns-raw}} prawns and set the meat aside. Fry the shells and heads in a little olive oil in a small pan for 3 minutes until pink and fragrant. Add {{tomato-puree}} tomato puree, stir for 1 minute, then add 1.2 litres of water. Simmer for 15 minutes. Strain and keep hot.
Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed. Add the hot prawn stock a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper.
Stir the peeled prawn meat into the risotto and cook for 90 seconds until just pink. Add {{parsley-flat}} parsley, stir once, and serve immediately.

items.cause: They were added too early or cooked too long.
items.fix: Prawns need only 90 seconds in a hot risotto. Add them right at the end, stir once or twice, and serve the moment they turn pink.

content.text: Prawn risotto appears along the entire Italian coastline. The Adriatic version, particularly from Venice and the Veneto, uses the prawn heads to make a quick stock rather than relying on bought fish stock. The result is a more orange, more intensely flavoured risotto than the version made with plain stock. Like all Italian seafood risotto, it is made without Parmesan.
